Area.evidence_source: This qualitative study has used a psychoanalyticallyinformed methodology to explore the experiences of four gay men in relation to their sexual orientation and suicidality. Suicide and homosexuality often remain taboo topics. Heteronormativity, as an organizing principle of social order, has over the years been reinforced by the legal–medical profession, compelling homosexuality to be at times hidden. While acknowledging the need for sensitive handling of suicidality among gay men and to avoid pathologizing, the issue of living as a gay man in a heterosexist culture must be given serious consideration as a potential precipitant of mental health problems.
